text:
maya: Heads-up — canary from yesterday shows weird tail latency spikes on model-v2 when kernel selection switches to the quant path. Anyone seen this pattern before?
jp: saw some noise in the logs, thought it was batching churn. do you have a snippet of the waterfall?
maya: pastes waterfall screenshot link -> https://img.redwood.local/xyz (private)
maya: spike aligns with KV cache misses in the same timeframe. token-level breakdown looks like the attention kernel hop is expensive for a subset of sequences.
sam: hm, are we seeing evictions? last week we changed the kv-ttl heuristic for long context seqs. could be thrash.
maya: yes — eviction rate jumps from ~0.5% to ~8% in the window.
rachel: curious — did the kernel routing rule change? the runtime now prefers quantized kernels when batch_size < 4 and seq_len < 512.
jp: that policy was added in rollout-67. might create oscillation for mixed workloads (short+long queries).
sam: quick reproduction plan: run short synthetic workload + occasional long shots to force switching. I can run on canary.
maya: please do. also want a dashboard to catch this earlier — a panel that shows per-route kernel-selection ratio + kv-eviction-rate over time.
jp: proposed prometheus queries: 
```
sum(rate(kernel_selection_total{kernel="quant"}[5m])) by (route)
/ sum(rate(kernel_selection_total[5m])) by (route)
```
plus:
```
sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) by (route)
```
maybe combine into a heatmap.
rachel: add token-level p50/p95/p99 for generation latency per route too. useful to correlate.
eval-bot: FYI — model-v2 A/B run 2024-06-01 produced 3.2% higher p99 token latency on canary vs control (auto-eval id: ae-20240601-92).
maya: thanks, that aligns. Can we add a panel that compares model-version ribbons by metric (p50/p95/p99 token-latency) and kernel mix?
jp: doable. dashboard layout idea: top row—per-route kernel mix (stacked area), second row—kv eviction rate + cache hit heatmap, third row—token latency waterfall (avg per token position), fourth row—model-version ribbons with small multiples.
sam: small request — include a toggle to filter for request size buckets (seq<256, 256-1024, >1024). kernel selection is sensitive to seq length.
rachel: +1. also surface rollout tags (canary/ab/control) so we can slice by cohort.
maya: can ops-bot create a temporary alert? Something like: if kv_evictions_total rate > 5% and quant_kernel_ratio > 60% for 10m, fire a pager to eng-runtime. We need early detection before p99 spikes.
ops-bot: @channel created alert rule "kv-thrash-quant-mix" -> severity=warning, notify=@eng-runtime-pager after 10m. (rule id: alert-8231) :white_check_mark:
jp: will wire an explainer panel linking to the root cause runbook (short checklist: check kernel policy change, check kv-ttl rollout, examine request size histogram, replay sample traces).
sam: running repro now on canary-3 (job id run-7742). I'll post logs if it reproduces.
maya: thanks. also let's capture a flame graph of the quant kernel during the spike — that may show surprising memcpy/copy path.
jp: note: when we switched to new compilation flags last month, we added a fallback path that does an extra copy for safety; maybe that hits on certain sequences.
rachel: if we confirm, we could add a fast-path guard for typical short sequences to avoid the extra copy. low-risk canary.
eval-bot: reminder — tie any kernel change to a mini-eval on latency-sensitive prompts. We had a silent regression last quarter because we only ran throughput tests.
maya: agreed. next steps: 1) sam runs repro and posts traces (ETA 30m). 2) jp builds dashboard panels (ETA 2d). 3) rachel drafts a kernel fast-path patch if repro confirmed (ETA 3d).
sam: repro logs -> ```
[2024-06-15T14:12:03Z] request id=6a2f kv_hit=false kernel=quant batch=1 seq=48 token=32 lat=18.7ms
[2024-06-15T14:12:03Z] request id=6a2f kv_load=miss fallback_copy=true memcpy=23ms
[2024-06-15T14:12:03Z] request id=6a2f trace_id=tr-112 flame_upload=http://telemetry/traces/tr-112
```
maya: flame graph link shows heavy memcpy in quant attention path. confirmed.
jp: opened a lightweight dashboard PR: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/fast/telemetry-kernel-compare (please review)
rachel: scanning the traces — the memcpy seems to come from alignment code when seq%16 != 0. quant kernels were optimized for 16-align blocks.
sam: that explains why only some sequences hit the high tail. our tokenizer sometimes produces off-by-ones for mixed-language prompts.
maya: suggestion: update kernel selection policy to prefer float kernel for sequences with seq%16 != 0 until we ship alignment fix. quick config change, low blast radius.
jp: rolled config change to canary-3: kernel_policy.override.route_regex="^/generate" prefer_kernel_for_unaligned="float". monitoring.
ops-bot: deploy canary config to canary-3 succeeded (deploy id cfg-551).
maya: initial telemetry after change — p99 down ~12% and kv_evictions stable. promising.
eval-bot: auto-eval rerun (ae-20240615-95) shows p99 delta now +0.1% vs control. good.
rachel: still want the alignment fix on roadmap. can we add a ticket?
maya: created ticket RW-3209 "quant kernel alignment optimization" and linked the traces.
sam: marking thread resolved for now — will keep watch for next 24h. please re-open if you see another spike. :+1:
maya: thanks all. copying a short TL;DR into eng-runtime-docs channel for visibility.
jp: nice follow-up: add a Grafana annotation stream for config rollouts so we can correlate spikes with config changes automatically.
rachel: agreed. smallops win.
maya: ok closing.
